sections.h2: Where the office is and when it's open
sections.html:
The Rutherford County Register of Deeds works from 229 North Main Street in Rutherfordton. Postal mail goes to Post Office Box 551, Rutherfordton, NC 28139. The counter is staffed from half past eight to five on weekdays, holidays excepted.

Two phone lines are published: 828-287-6155 for the main desk and 828-287-6195 for the record room. Holdings reach back into the 1700s, which helps anyone selling a family tract that has changed hands many times.

Most sellers never visit in person, because the attorney or title agent delivers the deed. If you do go, bring the original signed and notarized deed, the tax clearance and a way to pay the fee. Still, a rejected deed delays the closing and the payout, so the rules are worth knowing.

The register's collection covers a wide range of public records:

  • Real estate conveyances and deeds of trust, with their cancellations
  • Assumed names and powers of attorney
  • Road maintenance agreements and plats
  • Separation agreements and similar filings

An online index lets you search by name. A separate alert tool named Property Check emails you when something new is filed against a name or parcel you choose. Heirs watching a house that sits empty can use it to spot an unexpected lien or a forged transfer early. It costs nothing to set up, and it is worth doing as soon as you decide to sell a house nobody lives in.

Section 161-14 sets layout rules that a deed must meet on the page. Hold your draft up against each one:

  • Page one of a deed or deed of trust carries the preparer's name.
  • Paper is 8.5 inches wide and either 11 or 14 inches long.
  • Page one keeps its upper three inches empty, and every other edge needs at least half an inch of white space.
  • Text prints black on white, at 9 points or larger, on one side of each sheet.
  • The kind of instrument is spelled out across the head of page one.

Blanks and corrections may be inked in by hand. Having your attorney read the draft before signing is the cheapest way to dodge a rejected filing.

Late property tax will stop a deed from recording. Section 161-10(a)(19), effective October 1, 2011, makes payment of delinquent taxes a condition of recording.

A tax lien explains the rule. Under section 105-355 it fastens to the property on the listing date, and penalties, interest and costs fasten with it. If the debt goes unpaid, a foreclosure auction can follow, and a person who redeems before confirmation must pay all of it (section 105-374).

Request a written balance for every parcel from the Rutherford County revenue office before you sign a contract, so your attorney can clear it from the sale money. Do it early, since a balance you learn about on closing day can postpone the recording and the payout.

The statewide schedule in section 161-10 governs. On top of that, military discharges are recorded free and satisfactions of deeds of trust carry no charge.

Recording charges at the Rutherford County desk
DocumentFee
Standard instrument, pages 1 to 15$26.00 flat
Standard instrument, each page after 15$4.00
Mortgage or deed of trust, pages 1 to 35$64.00 flat
Mortgage or deed of trust, each page after 35$4.00
Deed of trust satisfactionNone
Military dischargeNone
Plat sheet$21.00

These are the only charges, and they are due before anything is filed.

The charge is one dollar per $500 of price or value, with leftover dollars rounded up to the next $500 block. The seller settles it before the deed is filed (section 105-228.30). The county keeps one half and the state receives the other.

A sale for cash is a transfer for value, so the tax is owed. Your attorney can show it as a separate line item.

Land that spans two counties is taxed in whichever county holds more of the value. If your Rutherford tract crosses a county line, raise it with your attorney early.

The statute also lets the county retain a small slice of the state half as an allowance, which is bookkeeping between governments.

The county revenue department answers tax bill questions at 828-287-6000. It sits at 145 College Avenue, Suite A, Rutherfordton, NC 28139, with counter hours of half past eight to five. A collections email address is posted on the department page.

All tax bills are due September 1 each year, and payment by January 5 avoids interest and enforced collection. Mailed payments are honored by postmark through that date. Cash or check payments are taken at the tax office. Online payment runs through a third-party service that adds its own fees.

The department page also offers a search for tax bill information, a link to registered vehicle tax receipts, and a list of delinquent tax bills. Pull your parcel's bill and ask for a payoff before your closing attorney orders the deed. Keep the payoff letter and the paid receipt together, because the title company will ask for both.

A tax rate document is posted too. Because the total bill depends on the fire district and town where the house sits, ask the office which rates apply to your parcel instead of assuming a countywide figure. Have the parcel number ready when you call.

The register of deeds records assumed business name certificates, the doing-business-as forms that tell the public a person or firm trades under a particular name in one county or in all 100 North Carolina counties. The recording fee is $26.00.

An online option exists for businesses located in Rutherford County, with a $15.00 service fee added to the recording fee. Landlords with rentals should make sure the business name used on their leases is still on file.

sections.h2: Electronic filing and why timing matters
sections.html:
E-recording through Simplifile began in the office on April 24, 2018, with plats added on February 1, 2022. Microfilming began January 1, 2017.

Speed matters because registration time sets rank. A deed or long lease binds lien creditors and later purchasers for value only from the moment it is registered, and the earlier filing wins (section 47-18). When a buyer's lender and a seller's lender both file on closing day, a same-day electronic filing keeps your deal clean.

Anyone unsure about a particular document can call the main desk at 828-287-6155 before sending it. Ask your attorney or title agent which method they will use, and when you can expect the recorded copy back, so you know when the buyer officially holds title.

faqs.q: What days is the Rutherford County recorder open?
faqs.a: Half past eight to five on weekdays, holidays excepted. The main line is 828-287-6155. Calling first avoids a wasted trip on a holiday week.

faqs.q: Is filing a deed of trust satisfaction free in Rutherford County?
faqs.a: Yes. No charge applies to satisfactions, and state law agrees. Make sure your lender files one after payoff.

faqs.q: Who owes deed excise tax when a Rutherford County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller does. Section 105-228.30 sets one dollar per $500, collected ahead of filing, and the settlement statement should show it as its own entry.

faqs.q: Can overdue taxes hold up my Rutherford County deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Under section 161-10(a)(19), back taxes come first. Obtain the balance from the revenue office and pay it at closing.

faqs.q: Does Rutherford County take electronic recordings?
faqs.a: Yes. E-recording via Simplifile started April 24, 2018, and plat e-recording started February 1, 2022. Title companies and attorneys generally use it.
